question: Whose autobiography is titled 'Waiting for a Visa' ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar** is the author of the autobiography titled **'Waiting for a Visa'**.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar is a prominent figure in Indian history, known for his role in the drafting of the Indian Constitution and his advocacy for the rights of the Dalits and other marginalized communities.
 
• 'Waiting for a Visa' is a short autobiographical account that highlights the discrimination and social injustices faced by Dr. Ambedkar and other members of the Dalit community.
 
• The autobiography provides a personal insight into the challenges and struggles faced by Dr. Ambedkar, which fueled his determination to fight for social justice and equality.
 
• This work is an important piece of literature that sheds light on the harsh realities of caste-based discrimination in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar** was born on 14th April 1891 and was an Indian jurist, economist, politician, and social reformer.
 
• He is also known as the principal architect of the Indian Constitution and served as the first Law Minister of independent India.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar's contributions to the upliftment of the marginalized communities in India are widely recognized and celebrated.
 
• He founded the **Dalit Buddhist Movement** and inspired the modern Buddhist movement in India.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar's legacy continues to influence social and political movements in India and around the world.
